FIX-A1 — UNNEST-WITH-ORDINALITY landing-point miss (HIGH).
  Defect: responder used `array_position(tags, tag)` for 'position of each tag while exploding' — WRONG semantics. array_position returns FIRST-occurrence index of a VALUE (verified at trino.io/docs/467/functions/array.html: 'Returns the position of the first occurrence of the element in array x (or 0 if not found)'), so duplicate tags collide (both 'billing' rows in ARRAY['billing','export','billing'] get position=1). Correct canonical = `CROSS JOIN UNNEST(arr) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(elem, ord)` — appends a 1-based bigint ordinality column at the END.

DOCS-TRUTH VERIFIED (WebFetch trino.io/docs/467) BEFORE WRITING:
  - array_position(x, element): 'Returns the position of the first occurrence of the element in array x (or 0 if not found).' 1-based, returns 0 (not NULL) when missing. First-match — duplicates collide. ✅
  - UNNEST ... WITH ORDINALITY: 'UNNEST can optionally have a WITH ORDINALITY clause, in which case an additional ordinality column is added to the end.' 1-based sequential integer (bigint) counter. Canonical form `CROSS JOIN UNNEST(arr) WITH ORDINALITY AS alias(col1, ..., ordinality_col)`. ✅
  - FROM-clause grammar: explicit CROSS JOIN keyword vs comma-separated implicit cross join are 'alternative syntaxes, not combinable forms.' `FROM t, CROSS JOIN u` violates the from_item grammar. ✅
